query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended as energetic structural materials, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release? State the proposed intervention, its hypothesized mechanism, the improvement expected relative to the untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Trace (≈0.3 at %) yttrium micro-alloying of a baseline equiatomic Ti–Zr–Nb–Hf–Ta refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA), followed by high-temperature homogenization, will increase room-temperature tensile ductility and strain hardening by ≥50 % without reducing (±5 %) ultimate strength or impact-induced exothermic energy release.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, equiatomic TiZrNbHfTa RHEA, single-phase BCC, homogenized 1200 °C / 24 h, water-quenched (≈3 % tensile elongation; ≈1100 MPa UTS; energetic burning in air on high-speed impact).
generation.intervention: Add 0.3 at % Y during melting, identical homogenization at 1200 °C for 24 h and water quench.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature quasi-static tension (10-3 s-1) and high-strain-rate (≈103 s-1) impact in laboratory air; bulk oxygen level <500 wppm.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale (≤2 nm) Y enrichment films along grain boundaries that scavenge O/N impurities and raise boundary cohesive energy.
generation.mechanism: Yttrium’s strong affinity for O/N draws embrittling interstitials out of BCC grain boundaries and reduces boundary energy, delaying intergranular crack nucleation; the cleaner, stronger boundaries emit and absorb dislocations more uniformly, raising work-hardening capacity while its low concentration leaves lattice strength and oxidation enthalpy essentially unchanged.
generation.predicted_outcome: Average tensile elongation ≥4.5 % (≥50 % rise) with UTS 1045-1155 MPa (±5 % of baseline); Charpy impact energy and post-impact combustion heat ≥95 % of baseline values.
generation.baseline: Same alloy and processing without Y addition.
generation.boundary: Effective for 0.1–0.6 at % Y and bulk O <500 wppm. Benefit disappears if Y >1 at % (oxide inclusions) or if final anneal <800 °C eliminates Y boundary segregation.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: limited published data on rare-earth micro-alloying in RHEAs and on its influence on high-rate oxidation chemistry.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce ≥3 replicate ingots of baseline and Y-doped alloys; confirm Y boundary segregation by atom-probe tomography; perform tensile tests (ASTM E8) and split-Hopkinson bar impact tests with in-situ pyrometry to quantify exothermic temperature rise.
measurements: Atom-probe Y concentration profile at grain boundaries
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if (a) elongation increase is <25 %, or (b) UTS drops >10 %, or (c) impact energy or exothermic heat release falls below 90 % of baseline, in ≥2 of 3 replicate comparisons.
